questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Position Vector of a Particle Moving With Constant Acceleration
questions.problem: A particle moves from the origin with an acceleration of $(2i-4j)\,{\text{in/s}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(i-2j)\,\text{in/s}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $3$ seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

 

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=0i+0j,\,u=i-2j,\,a=2i-4j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=3\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(0i+0j)+(i-2j)(3)+\frac{1}{2}(2i-4j)(3)^{2} \\  & =(3i-6j)+9(i-2j) \\  & =(3i-6j)+(9i-18j) \\  & =(12i-24j)\,\text{in}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Distance Between a Particle and the Origin
questions.problem: A particle moves from the origin with an acceleration of $(-2i+j)\,{\text{ft/s}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(4i+j)\,\text{ft/s}.$ Find the distance from the particle to the origin after $4$ seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

 

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=0i+0j,\,u=4i+j,\,a=-2i+j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=4\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(0i+0j)+(4i+j)(4)+\frac{1}{2}(-2i+j)(4)^{2} \\  & =(16i+4j)+8(-2i+j) \\  & =(16i+4j)+(-16i+8j) \\  & =12j\,\text{ft}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance from the particle to the origin at this time is

$$
\begin{aligned}|r| & =|12j| \\  & =|12| \\  & =12\,\text{ft}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A delivery drone starts from the point with position vector $(1i+2j)\,\text{mi}$ and moves with a constant velocity of $(3i-2j)\,\text{mi/h}.$ Determine the distance $(|r|)$ from the drone to the origin after $3$ hours.

$\,|r|=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{mi}$
questions.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant velocity $u,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut,
$$

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=1i+2j,\,u=3i-2j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the drone after $t=3\,\text{h}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & ={r}_{0}+ut \\  & =(1i+2j)+(3i-2j)(3) \\  & =(1i+2j)+(9i-6j) \\  & =(10i-4j)\,\text{mi}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance from the drone to the origin at this time is

$$
\begin{aligned}|r| & =|10i-4j| \\  & =\sqrt{{10}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{100+16} \\  & =\sqrt{116} \\  & =2\sqrt{29}\,\text{mi}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
An object moves from the origin with an acceleration of $(-2i+4j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(3i+j)\,\text{m/s}.$ Find the distance from the object to the origin$(|r|)$ after $2$ seconds.

$\,|r|=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{m}$
questions.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=0i+0j,\,u=3i+j,\,a=-2i+4j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the object after $t=2\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(0i+0j)+(3i+j)(2)+\frac{1}{2}(-2i+4j)(2)^{2} \\  & =(6i+2j)+\frac{1}{2}(-8i+16j) \\  & =(6i+2j)+(-4i+8j) \\  & =(2i+10j)\,\text{m}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance from the object to the origin at this time is

$$
\begin{aligned}|r| & =|2i+10j| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{10}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+100} \\  & =\sqrt{104} \\  & =2\sqrt{26}\,\text{m}.\end{aligned}
$$
